title: function-output-attachment-base64-truncation-via-proxy-dedicated-escalation
creator: Alex Chen
description: Multiple enterprise customers (notably FinBank Inc. on Dedicated and two Private VPC customers) reported production failures where function/tool call responses containing base64-encoded attachments intermittently fail JSON parsing in our server-side handler. Failures manifest as invalid base64 padding or truncated payloads at the end of the encoded blob, leading to function invocation errors and downstream application failures.
steps_to_reproduce: Customer issues function call that returns JSON with an 'attachments' array where file contents are base64 encoded (large > 256KB).

Request passes through customer's private proxy or our Dedicated gateway when connection uses Transfer-Encoding: chunked and the gateway rewrites headers to include Content-Length for upstream processing.

When the response body is reassembled, the final chunk boundary conversion occasionally drops trailing '=' padding characters or a final '\n' in the body, producing malformed base64 inside the JSON string.
Server-side structured output parser attempts to decode attachment field, fails with invalid padding error, and the request is marked as failed.
observed_behavior: JSON parse / base64 decode errors on function outputs for large attachments in Hosted/Dedicated/Private when a proxy/gateway performs chunked->non-chunked reassembly. Intermittent across requests, correlates with specific proxy configurations and presence of trailing newlines in tool output.
expected_behavior: The gateway and runtime should preserve exact byte-for-byte response body from the model/tool execution so JSON/base64 integrity is maintained; parser should also fail gracefully and produce a clear error and automated retry path.
logs: 2026-03-02T14:12:33Z ERROR runtime/parse.go:215 base64 decode failed: illegal base64 data at input byte 131072
2026-03-02T14:12:33Z WARN gateway/rewrite.go:98 chunked->length rewrite dropped trailing delimiter for connection id=abcd-1234
2026-03-03T09:41:07Z ERROR private-agent/handler.go:402 structured response parse error: invalid padding
Example customer payload snippet: {"attachments":[{"filename":"report.pdf","data":"JVBERi0xLjQKJc... (truncated) ...Q=="}]} (note last '==' sometimes missing)
root_cause_summary: Our gateway's header rewrite and chunk reassembly logic attempted to normalize Transfer-Encoding headers by computing Content-Length and concatenating chunks. Under certain timing/edge conditions the code trimmed a trailing '\n' or final chunk boundary bytes when concatenating buffers, which removed 1-2 bytes from the end of base64-encoded strings embedded in JSON. This makes the base64 invalid and causes the parser to fail. The issue is triggered more often for large attachment payloads and when intermediate proxies add or remove chunk metadata.
temporary_mitigation: 1) Instructed impacted customers to enable passthrough (no header rewrite) on their proxies where possible. 2) Deployed emergency guard in runtime that detects malformed base64 in attachment fields and attempts a best-effort heuristic: append padding ('=') up to 2 bytes and re-decode; if still failing, return structured error that surfaces exact failure to customers with a suggested retry. 3) Added alerting dashboard to track base64 decode error rate.
permanent_fix_summary: 1) Fix gateway chunked->length reassembly to preserve exact bytes and avoid trimming delimiters. 2) Add end-to-end checksum (SHA256) for 'attachment' objects in tool responses so we can validate integrity before decode. 3) Harden structured output parser to fail with an actionable error that supports automated retry with fallback model variant. 4) Add integration tests and fuzzing across proxy header permutations.
